title: Good works and sins differ in their whole kind
source_text: X. Tantum abest ut ista, & similia piorum opera, quae per Dei gratiam & auxilium praestant, inter peccata numeremus, ut illa a peccatis toto genere discrepare libenter agnoscamus. Siquidem peccata lege divina prohibentur: Opera vero quae fideles per Dei gratiam faciunt lege praecipiuntur. Peccata Deo displicent, & sunt ipsi odio & abominationi: Opera vero piorum Deus amat, & eis delectatur. Illa Deus severe vindicat: haec vero secundum suam bonitatem remuneratur. Illa obstant hominis saluti: haec vero inter media salutis locum habent, & sunt via ad salutem a Deo praeparata. Illa minime Deum authorem habent, sed pravam voluntatem daemonis & hominis: haec vero sunt Deo ascribenda & fiunt spiritu illius movente. Denique per illa profanatur & blasphematur Dei nomen: per haec vero sanctificatur atque glorificatur.
pass_a_gloss: X. So far is it from our numbering these, & similar works of the godly, which they perform through the grace & help of God, among sins, that we willingly acknowledge that they differ from sins in their whole kind. For sins are forbidden by the divine law: But the works which the faithful do through the grace of God are commanded by the law. Sins displease God, & are a hatred & abomination to him: But the works of the godly God loves, & delights in them. The former God severely punishes: but the latter he rewards according to his goodness. The former stand in the way of man's salvation: but the latter have a place among the means of salvation, & are the way to salvation prepared by God. The former by no means have God as author, but the depraved will of the devil & of man: but the latter are to be ascribed to God & are done by his spirit moving. Finally by the former the name of God is profaned & blasphemed: but by the latter it is sanctified & glorified.
pass_b_english: Thesis X. Far from counting these and similar works of the godly, done with God's grace and help, among sins, we gladly acknowledge that they are a different kind of thing altogether.

God's law forbids sins, but it commands the works believers do by his grace. Sins displease God and he hates and abhors them; the works of the godly he loves and takes delight in. Sins he punishes severely; good works he rewards out of his goodness. Sins block a person's salvation; good works are among the means of salvation and are the road to it that God has prepared.

Sins do not have God as their author at all, but the corrupt will of the devil and of human beings; good works are to be credited to God and are done as his Spirit moves us. Finally, sins profane and blaspheme God's name, while good works hallow and glorify it.

are done by his spirit moving

choices.english: nor are they to be called sins
choices.why: Le Blanc rejects the claim that the good works of believers are sins.
rejected: nor should they be named sins
nor may they be styled offences
